name: dns
description: DNS from the stub to the root and back: referrals and glue, an iterative trace, a validating resolver's upstream queries and cache, a record change and a negative answer followed through the cache, NODATA, truncation, lame and dead delegations, DNSSEC secure/insecure/bogus, REFUSED, split-horizon views, and glibc's search list, ndots, timeouts and /etc/hosts

checks.name: ask a root server directly (no recursion): it does not know app.shop.test, it refers us to test.
the test. server refers us to shop.test., with glue
the shop.test. server answers with authority (aa)
dnslab trace does the same walk automatically, as a resolver would
a CNAME into another zone sends the trace back to the root, and lands in corp.test's external view
a cold cache: the resolver asks root, test. and shop.test. — QNAME-minimised — and fetches DNSKEYs to validate
asked again: answered from cache, nothing goes upstream
the public resolver caches it too, a few seconds later than the office resolver
change app.shop.test from .10 to .20 on the authoritative server (edit the zone, bump the serial, rndc reload)
run: sed -i 's/^app\t10\tA\t198.18.70.10/app\t10\tA\t198.18.70.20/' /etc/bind/shop.test.db && sed -i 's/hostmaster.shop.test. [0-9]*/hostmaster.shop.test. 2/' /etc/bind/shop.test.db && rndc reload shop.test && grep -E '^(app|new)' /etc/bind/shop.test.db

checks.name: follow it: the authority answers .20 at once; each resolver keeps .10 until its cached copy's TTL runs out
a name that does not exist yet: NXDOMAIN, with the zone's SOA in the authority section
the negative TTL comes from the SOA: min(SOA TTL 20, MINIMUM 3600) = 20 s
expect_contains: negative answer cacheable for 20 s = min(SOA TTL 20, MINIMUM 3600)

checks.name: now create new.shop.test
run: printf 'new\t10\tA\t198.18.70.60\n' >> /etc/bind/shop.test.db && sed -i 's/hostmaster.shop.test. [0-9]*/hostmaster.shop.test. 3/' /etc/bind/shop.test.db && rndc reload shop.test && grep -E '^(app|new)' /etc/bind/shop.test.db

checks.name: the resolver keeps answering NXDOMAIN until its negative entry expires (at most 20 s)
NODATA is different: the name exists, there is just no AAAA record; NOERROR with an empty answer
a 1.6 KB TXT answer does not fit the 1232-byte EDNS buffer: truncated over UDP, repeated over TCP
a lame delegation: broken.test. points at a server that does not serve it; the resolver answers SERVFAIL
a dead delegation: slow.test.'s only server is unreachable; the client times out before the resolver gives up
run: s=$(date +%s%N); dig +tries=1 +time=4 www.slow.test A; rc=$?; echo "exit $rc after $(( ($(date +%s%N) - s) / 1000000 )) ms"

checks.name: keep asking (one try, 2 s each): the client sees timeouts until the resolver gives up on the server, then SERVFAIL at once
run: s=$(date +%s); for i in $(seq 60); do r=$(dig +tries=1 +time=2 www2.slow.test | grep -oE "status: [A-Z]+|timed out" | head -1); echo "$(( $(date +%s) - s ))s: $r"; case "$r" in status*) break;; esac; sleep 1; done; s=$(date +%s%N); dig +tries=1 +time=2 www3.slow.test | grep -o "status: [A-Z]*"; rc=$?; echo "exit $rc after $(( ($(date +%s%N) - s) / 1000000 )) ms"

checks.name: a signed zone validates: the ad flag (authenticated data)
an unsigned zone (no DS in its parent) is insecure, not broken: an answer without ad
expired signatures: the validating resolver refuses to answer — SERVFAIL, with an Extended DNS Error
+cd (checking disabled) gets the data anyway: proof the failure is validation, not reachability
the office resolver only serves the office subnet: REFUSED
split horizon, inside: the office resolver is in corp.test's internal view
split horizon, outside: the same names through the public resolver
the stub's configuration: a search list and Kubernetes' ndots:5
getent ahosts app.shop.test (2 dots < 5): both search suffixes are tried first, then the name itself
with a trailing dot the name is absolute: one query
a dead first nameserver (timeout:2): every lookup waits 2 s before the second server answers — glibc caches nothing
run:
printf 'nameserver 198.18.53.2
nameserver 198.18.60.2
options timeout:2 attempts:2
' > /etc/resolv.conf; cat /etc/resolv.conf; for i in 1 2; do s=$(date +%s%N); getent ahosts app.shop.test >/dev/null; rc=$?; echo "exit $rc after $(( ($(date +%s%N) - s) / 1000000 )) ms"; done

checks.name: /etc/hosts wins: getent (via nsswitch 'files dns') sees it, dig never reads it
run: printf 'nameserver 198.18.60.2\n' > /etc/resolv.conf; cat /etc/resolv.conf; grep legacy /etc/hosts; getent hosts legacy.corp.test; dig legacy.corp.test | grep -o 'status: [A-Z]*'

checks.name: Go's own resolver reads the same files (GODEBUG=netdns=go+1 says which resolver it chose)
run: GODEBUG=netdns=go+1 ${BIN}/dnslab lookup legacy.corp.test 2>&1; GODEBUG=netdns=go+1 ${BIN}/dnslab lookup app.shop.test 2>&1
